facts.text: Budapest’s Parliament Building and Matthias Church are Neo‑Gothic landmarks that reuse original Romanesque stone from 1015.
The historic center along the Danube earned UNESCO World Heritage status for its 13th‑century Matthias Church, Buda Castle, and 19th‑century Parliament.
Budapest hosts the world’s second‑largest synagogue, the third‑largest parliament building, over 40 museums, and nearly ten Michelin‑starred restaurants.
In December 2015, Budapest was named a UNESCO City of Design and has been part of the Creative Cities Network ever since.
The Magyar tribes, led by Árpád, settled the Buda–Pest area in the late 9th century, later founding the Kingdom of Hungary.
Budapest is home to Gül Baba’s tomb, the northernmost site of an influential Islamic Turkish Sufi Dervish in Europe.
